# dotfiles

Home Manager configuration for `sauyon`.

## New machine setup

For a blank machine (ISO, disk, base Arch install), see
[docs/new-host.md](docs/new-host.md). The steps below assume Arch is already
running.

```bash
# 1. Clone into ~/devel/dotfiles
mkdir -p ~/devel
git clone https://github.com/sauyon/dotfiles ~/devel/dotfiles

# 2. If this is a new host, add a homeConfigurations entry for it in flake.nix
#    (hostname, gui, gpu). Otherwise the matching entry already exists.

# 3. Install Nix
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf -L https://install.determinate.systems/nix \
  | sudo sh -s -- install --no-confirm

# 4. Source Nix and trust mise
. /nix/var/nix/profiles/default/etc/profile.d/nix-daemon.sh
mise trust ~/devel/dotfiles/mise.toml

# 5. Apply (flake attr matches hostname)
nix run github:nix-community/home-manager -- switch --flake ~/devel/dotfiles#$HOST
```

After the first switch, `home-manager switch` is available directly.

## Applying changes: `hms`

`hms` is the normal way to switch. It does **not** build locally by default — it
pushes, waits for the commit's CI run, then switches, which turns the switch into
a download of the closure the runner already built and pushed to attic.

```bash
hms              # push, wait for the run, then switch
hms --local      # skip CI and build here (the old `home-manager switch` alias)
```

Things it deliberately refuses rather than works around:

- **A dirty tree.** CI builds a pushed commit, so an uncommitted switch is one CI
  can never reproduce. Commit, or use `--local`.
- **A stale checkout.** If `origin/master` has commits you do not, it says so and
  stops — rebasing is your call, and waiting on a run for a SHA that is not
  `origin/master` would be waiting on the wrong build.

It falls back to a local build, with a note, when the host has no CI job (mari)
or when the commit touched nothing `nix-home.yml`'s `paths:` filter matches. On a
red run it prints the job's actual `error:` lines, not just a status.

Why this is worth a wait: see `docs/ci-nix-home.md`. The short version is that
the runner has far more of everything than these boxes, and its output is
bit-identical to what a local build would produce.

## Tests

Nothing here has a suite; the exception is anything whose logic is a model of
someone else's, where a comment claiming the model is right proves nothing.

```bash
./tests/hyprlock-faillock.sh     # builds the script, then drives 33 cases
./tests/system-packages.sh       # sources system/pacman.sh, drives 21 cases
./tests/thermald-setup.sh        # drives 8 cases against system/thermald-setup
./tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh   # drives 13 cases against the live generated zsh config
./tests/steam-ui-scaling.sh      # evaluates 3 hosts, drives 4 cases
./tests/steam-env.sh             # builds the steam wrapper, drives 39 cases
```

`hyprlock-faillock` (in `home.nix`) reproduces pam_faillock's two tally windows
to tell the lock screen whether the account is locked out. The cases drive the
real built script through its `FAILLOCK_BIN` / `FAILLOCK_CONF` / `FAILLOCK_USER`
seams, so a stub reader supplies synthetic tally records -- no real failed
logins, no waiting out a real ten-minute lockout.

`system/pacman.sh` holds the parts of `system/deploy`'s package convergence that
model someone else's rules: the list format plus the per-host overlay, and the
single `Include` line appended to `/etc/pacman.conf` (whole-line matched, so the
stock config's commented-out examples don't read as "already enabled"). The
cases source it and run against a temp tree through its `SUDO` seam, then hand a
copy of this host's real `pacman.conf` to `pacman-conf` to confirm pacman does
glob an `Include` and does register a `[multilib]` section reached through one --
the assumption the whole drop-in design rests on. Nothing writes to `/etc`, and
no case needs root.

`system/thermald-setup` (run from `system/deploy`) is the *enable* half that a
package list cannot express: `pacman -S` installs a unit, it does not start one.
Which hosts want thermald is decided upstream of it, by `thermald` appearing in
`system/packages.<host>` — so the script's own gate is just "is it installed",
and a host whose list never asked for it is one it never touches. The cases drive
the real script with stub `pacman`/`sudo`/`systemctl` on `PATH`, asserting both
halves: a host without the package does nothing at all, and a converged host
escalates zero times.

The `_ghostty_saved_ps1` priming in `zsh.nix` is a model of ghostty's
`ghostty-integration`: it pre-sets variables private to that script so its own
`ps1_changed` guard fires on the first precmd, which is what stops the PS1
rewrite that corrupts powerlevel10k's `PROMPT` into a literal `}}`. Rename those
variables upstream and nix still builds, `hms` still succeeds, and the only
symptom is the artifact coming back. The cases render the *live generated* config
in a pty -- both the injected and plain startup paths -- and assert the `}}` is
gone with the line and still returns without it, so a workaround that has quietly
stopped working fails out loud, and so does one that has become unnecessary.

`STEAM_FORCE_DESKTOPUI_SCALING` (in `home.nix`) models Steam's side of a bargain
Hyprland can't enforce: `xwayland.force_zero_scaling` hands X11 clients real
pixels and no DPI hint, and Steam's CEF UI reads neither `Xft.dpi` nor
`GDK_DPI_SCALE`, so on a scaled panel it draws tiny until told its own factor.
The cases evaluate three hosts and derive every expectation from the config
itself — the var must equal the scale that host's eDP-1 monitor rule asks for,
and be unset where there is no such rule — so the pair can't drift apart
silently, which is the only way this fails. A fourth case asserts a scaled host
still exists, since otherwise all three would pass vacuously.

The `steam` wrapper (in `home.nix`) and `home/steam-desktop-override` model the two
places nix's profile and a pacman-installed app collide. Steam shells out to
`xdg-user-dir`, `~/.nix-profile/bin` precedes `/usr/bin`, and nix's loader can't
satisfy what Arch's `libc.so.6` leaves undefined — `__pointer_chk_guard`; and
`GIO_EXTRA_MODULES` points Steam's sniper runtime at a gvfs module its older glib
can't load. The wrapper prepends the host's directories rather than sanitising nix
away, because `xdg-open` exists *only* in the profile here and is how Steam opens a
link, so the cases assert both directions — a fix that satisfies one and breaks the
other looks correct from either side alone. Three of them are there because the
obvious assertion passes with the bug still in place: the `xdg-user-dir` case reads
through `readlink` (profile entries are symlinks, so the unresolved name is never a
store path), the `xdg-open` case *executes* it rather than resolving it (a `command
-v` check can only fail when the case above it already has), and a first case
asserts the `/usr/bin`-vs-profile collision still exists at all, without which the
rest can pass having measured nothing. The `nix eval` cases cover the wiring, since
the wrapper and the script can both be correct while the activation entry passes the
wrong paths — including that the entry keeps its `|| warnEcho`, because activation
runs under `set -eu` and a bare failure here would abort the entries after it.

## System config

Files under `system/` mirror `/` and require root to deploy:

```bash
system/deploy
```

`system/packages` is the pacman list every Arch host must satisfy;
`system/packages.<hostname>` is layered on it for one box (shiori's `steam` and
its 32-bit drivers). Deploy converges pacman onto both on every run, and enables
multilib via `system/etc/pacman.d/conf.d/multilib.conf` plus one `Include` in
`/etc/pacman.conf`. A newly enabled repo has no sync db, so the first deploy
after this asks for a `sudo pacman -Syu` rather than refreshing behind your back
(`-Sy` without the `-u` is the partial-upgrade footgun).

## Storage tuning

One-shot tuning for the btrfs-on-LUKS-on-loop-on-ext4 home stack: sets LUKS
workqueue-bypass flags, `noatime` on host `/home`, grows btrfs into LUKS
device slack. Idempotent. The LUKS step prompts for the passphrase.

```bash
system/storage-tuning.sh
```

## Secrets (sops-nix)

Secrets are decrypted using `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` as an age identity. On a new machine, either copy your existing key or generate one and add it as a sops recipient:

```bash
# Add new machine key as recipient
cd ~/devel/dotfiles
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
mise run sops -- updatekeys secrets.yaml
```

input.command:
git add -A && git commit -q --amend -F - <<'MSG'
home: launch Steam through a wrapper that prefers the host's helpers

Steam is the pacman package, but it inherits a PATH whose first entry is
~/.nix-profile/bin, and that breaks it in one measured way. Steam shells out to
`xdg-user-dir <key>` (the string in steamclient.so is the format `xdg-user-dir %s`)
to locate a user directory; xdg.userDirs.enable puts nix's xdg-user-dirs in the
profile, so the call lands on the nix copy. Measured on shiori 2026-09-28, once per
launch:

  xdg-user-dir: symbol lookup error: /usr/lib/libc.so.6: undefined symbol:
  __pointer_chk_guard, version GLIBC_PRIVATE

The mechanism is a mismatched loader/libc pair, and it runs the opposite way to what
the message suggests at a glance. Measured with `nm -D`: Arch's ld.so *defines*
__pointer_chk_guard@@GLIBC_PRIVATE and Arch's libc.so.6 (2.44) leaves it *undefined*,
expecting its own loader to supply it; nix's glibc 2.42 defines it in neither. The nix
binary keeps nix's hardcoded ELF interpreter, Steam's runtime puts Arch's
/usr/lib/libc.so.6 in its library path, and nix's older loader cannot satisfy that
newer libc's reference -- which is why the error names /usr/lib/libc.so.6 as the
referrer rather than the binary.

The fix prepends the host's directories rather than sanitising nix out of PATH, and
the difference is load-bearing: `xdg-open` exists ONLY in the profile here, because
Arch's xdg-utils is not installed, and it is how Steam opens a link. That it *works*
from there is a second fact worth recording, because nix's xdg-open dies identically
under a Steam-runtime library path. steam.sh saves this wrapper's environment as
SYSTEM_PATH/SYSTEM_LD_LIBRARY_PATH (:135-136) and steamclient.so, which references
both names, restores them for an external handler. Not steam.sh:1015 -- that restore
is on the restart path, feeding the MAGIC_RESTART_EXITCODE re-exec, and an earlier
draft of this commit miscited it. It does mean the tray's restart re-execs
/usr/bin/steam with SYSTEM_PATH, i.e. this wrapper's already-prepended PATH, so the
fix survives that too.

The cost, stated because it is larger than the fix: this reorders name resolution for
Steam's whole descendant tree, not just Steam -- games, Proton helpers, anything a
launch option invokes, and via SYSTEM_PATH the external handlers too. Nothing is
removed, and the reordering runs toward root-owned directories (/usr/local/bin and
/usr/bin are root:root here; ~/.nix-profile/bin is under $HOME). A shim directory
holding only xdg-user-dir would scope it tighter; prepending is preferred because it
needs no list of which helpers to redirect, and that list is what would rot.

GIO_EXTRA_MODULES (env.nix) is unset for a related reason: steamwebhelper logged
`libgvfscommon.so: undefined symbol: g_task_set_static_name` twice per launch. The
host is not part of this -- Arch's glib2 is 2.88.3, the same version nix's gvfs is
built against, and it exports the symbol. g_task_set_static_name landed in glib 2.76,
while the runtime that logged it (steamrt64/pv-runtime, steamrt3c, which is what the
journal names) ships 2.66.8 and the scout runtime the 32-bit client runs under ships
2.58.3. An earlier draft blamed "sniper"; this install has none, steam.sh rm -fr's it
as "now replaced by steamrt3c". Steam's UI is CEF, not GTK, so the volume monitor
that variable exists for buys Steam nothing. Unset by name, not by a GIO_* sweep.

home/steam-desktop-override is the other half: elephant/walker and xdg-open exec the
desktop file's Exec= line, not $PATH. It rewrites the pacman file at activation
instead of mirroring it -- steam.desktop is 282 lines, a Comment= plus 26 translations
then nine Desktop Actions (eight with 26 translations of their own Name=) -- and only
the ten Exec= need to differ.

Its failure policy is the part that took the most getting right. The generated
`activate` runs under `set -eu` (verified: line 2 of a built generation), and this
entry sorts after linkGeneration and reloadSystemd but BEFORE zenInstallsIni. A bare
non-zero exit would therefore not merely skip the launcher fix: it would abort the
rest of activation, leaving the profile already pointing at the new generation while
gcroots/current-home still names the old one, and leaving installs.ini for Zen to
re-pin. So the call site appends `|| warnEcho` and degrades to "Steam launches
unwrapped" -- the same call system/deploy makes with `./thermald-setup || echo ...
continuing`.

Five ways this could have failed silently, each now loud:
  - A source whose Exec= shape changed matched nothing, and a verbatim copy got
    installed at a path that OUTRANKS /usr/share -- the original bug, behind a file
    that looks like the fix. Refused by a post-condition.
  - A PARTIAL rewrite passed that post-condition: the real file has ten Exec= lines,
    and an update changing only the nine Desktop Action ones would leave every
    right-click action unwrapped while the main entry satisfied "did anything get
    rewritten?". Now no line that looks like a target may survive -- and the survivor
    class is "the name ends here", not "a space follows", because the first version of
    that check let a tab-separated survivor through. Its own test case caught that.
  - The no-Steam branch left a stale override forever; after GC the launcher entry
    still looks right and does nothing. Now removed -- keyed on a marker line the
    script writes, NOT on guessing `-steam` in the store path, which would have
    stopped matching the moment the wrapper derivation were renamed.
  - "Not a readable regular file" was treated as "this host has no Steam", so a
    directory or a bad mode could delete a working override. Those are now separated:
    genuinely absent is the quiet path, anything else is an error.
  - The temp sweep globbed `.??????`, exactly six characters, and so deleted a user's
    steam.desktop.backup on every hms. The template carries an `hm-` infix now.

tests/steam-env.sh drives both halves plus the home.nix wiring through 42 cases, and
every guard was checked against a mutation that should break it -- 21 in total, and
the mutation log is the reason several of the above exist. Two mutations changed no
case's result, and both were findings rather than weak tests: a separate emptiness
check was dead code (the post-condition already refuses an empty source) and is gone,
and of the three metacharacter cases only whitespace needs the up-front validation,
which the comment now says.

Five cases exist because the obvious assertion passes with the bug still in place:
the xdg-user-dir case reads through readlink (profile entries are symlinks, so the
unresolved name is never a store path); the xdg-open case executes it rather than
resolving it (a `command -v` check can only fail when the case above it already has);
a first case asserts the collision still exists at all; the wiring case compares
argument ORDER, since checking that each path merely appears somewhere passes a
src/dst transposition; and the fixture wrapper path deliberately does not end in
`-steam`, so the marker predicate cannot be satisfied by luck.

---
name: drovr-panel-flaky-angles
description: "drovr code-review's correctness/type-design reviewers often die or emit degenerate output; cover the angle with a read-only Explore agent instead of re-running"
metadata:
  type: project
---

In the dotfiles repo (2026-09-28 session), `drovr code-review run` lost the
`correctness` angle three rounds running and `type-design` once. The reviewer
panes vanished ("herdr says no such pane") or the backend — shown in the pane
footer as `google/gemma-4-31b-it` — emitted thousands of repeated `S-S-S-`
tokens and truncated. Each loss is recorded as a stand-in **Critical**, so the
panel returns exit 3 and never converges.

**Why:** the skill's own termination rule says two consecutive rounds that lose
a dimension end the loop on a record, not a verdict — re-running past that
burns ~10 minutes per round and measures nothing.

**How to apply:** after the second lost round, dispatch a read-only `Explore`
agent for the missing angle with an explicit brief (range, working-tree state,
severity ratings, findings inline not written to disk). That substitute found
two real Importants the panel never would have. Also re-check
`git rev-parse master` before trusting any verdict — see
[[dotfiles-master-moves-under-you]].

---
name: drovr-panel-flaky-angles
description: "drovr code-review's panel often loses angles, and in a plain Claude Code session it cannot start at all (HERDR_SOCKET_PATH unset); cover the angles with read-only Explore agents"
metadata:
  type: project
---

In the dotfiles repo, `drovr code-review run` has failed two different ways.

**Whole panel unavailable (2026-09-28, second session).** It exits immediately
with `drovr: code-review run failed: HERDR_SOCKET_PATH is not set; cannot reach
herdr socket` — 0 of 4 angles, no artifacts beyond the run dir. `drovr new` warns
about the same thing (`could not create herdr workspace`). So outside a herdr
pane the panel is not degraded, it is absent.

**Individual angles dying (earlier session).** It lost `correctness` three rounds
running and `type-design` once: panes vanished ("herdr says no such pane") or the
backend (`google/gemma-4-31b-it`, shown in the pane footer) emitted thousands of
repeated `S-S-S-` tokens and truncated. Each loss records a stand-in
**Critical**, so the panel returns exit 3 and never converges.

**Why:** the skill's termination rule says two consecutive rounds that lose a
dimension end the loop on a record, not a verdict — re-running past that burns
~10 minutes per round and measures nothing. With no herdr socket there is
nothing to re-run at all.

**How to apply:** don't budget on the panel in a plain session — go straight to
read-only `Explore` agents, one per angle (correctness, security,
error-handling, verification/quality), each briefed with the explicit range
(`<base>..HEAD` **plus** whether the working tree is clean), told to rate every
finding Critical/Important/nit and to report inline rather than write files.
Four such agents on an ~880-line change returned 1 Critical and 10 Importants
the panel never saw, including three comments that stated a mechanism backwards.
Ask them to *verify claims against the machine*, not just read the diff — that
is what caught the inverted `__pointer_chk_guard` story. Also re-check
`git rev-parse master` before trusting any verdict — see
[[dotfiles-master-moves-under-you]].

input.description: Round 3 correctness review
input.prompt:
You are a READ-ONLY skeptical reviewer (correctness + robustness). Write nothing — no files, no mutating git commands. Review as a skeptic, not the author.

Repo: /home/sauyon/devel/dotfiles/.drovr/wt/steam-nix-env (git worktree, branch drovr/steam-nix-env). Working tree is clean.
Range: `git diff 10fabaf..HEAD` — one commit, 814e4fa.

This is ROUND 3. Rounds 1 and 2 found a Critical and ten Importants, all now fixed. Your job is to review the CURRENT state, with particular suspicion of the round-2 fixes themselves, which no reviewer has seen. Do not assume a fix is correct because it is a fix — one round-2 fix already shipped with a real bug (a survivor check written `( |$)` that missed a tab-separated survivor), found only by its own test case.

What changed since round 2, all in home/steam-desktop-override unless noted:
1. Stale-override detection now writes and greps a MARKER comment line (`# generated by dotfiles home/steam-desktop-override -- do not edit`) prepended to the output, instead of guessing `^Exec=/nix/store/[^/]*-steam/bin/steam`.
2. Post-condition gained a second half: refuse if any `^Exec=/usr/bin/steam([^A-Za-z0-9_.-]|$)` SURVIVES the rewrite (catches a partial rewrite), in addition to requiring at least one rewritten line.
3. The `[ ! -e "$src" ]` (genuinely absent → quiet cleanup, now with a stderr notice) path is split from "present but not a readable regular file" (→ error, exit 1).
4. Temp template changed from `$dst.XXXXXX` to `$dst.hm-XXXXXX`, and the sweep from `"$dst".??????` to `"$dst".hm-??????` (the bare glob was eating steam.desktop.backup).
5. `$exe` whitelist widened to include `?` and `=`.
6. home.nix: wrapper comment rewritten (mechanism claims corrected); activation entry unchanged in behaviour.
7. tests/steam-env.sh: now 42 cases, including argument-ORDER assertion on the activation entry, an `mv`-is-rename symlink case, an absent-PATH case, and a partial-rewrite case.

Hunt specifically for:
- THE MARKER. Is prepending a `#` comment line before `[Desktop Entry]` actually valid per the Desktop Entry spec, and do real launchers (and `xdg-open`/desktop-file-utils) accept a file whose first line is a comment? If a comment before the first group header is NOT valid, this silently breaks every launch. Check the spec and if possible `desktop-file-validate` the produced file.
- The survivor regex `^Exec=/usr/bin/steam([^A-Za-z0-9_.-]|$)`. Trace it against: `Exec=/usr/bin/steam`, `Exec=/usr/bin/steam %U`, `Exec=/usr/bin/steam<TAB>x`, `Exec=/usr/bin/steamfoo`, `Exec=/usr/bin/steam-native`, `Exec=/usr/bin/steam.sh`, `Exec=/usr/bin/steam/`, `Exec=/usr/bin/steam2`. Which are correctly classified and which are wrong? Is excluding `.` and `-` right, or does it create a false negative (a real unrewritten target that slips through)?
- Interaction between the marker and idempotency: re-running reads $src (no marker) so output has exactly one marker — but what if someone points `$src` AT a previously-generated override (e.g. a mistaken config, or the transposition bug)? Does the marker double up, and does anything detect it?
- The `rm -f "$dst".hm-??????` glob: any remaining case where it deletes something it should not, or fails (directory match, permissions) and takes the `warnEcho` path?
- The split `-e` / `-f`+`-r` logic: is there a state that falls through both branches wrongly? Dangling symlink at $src? Symlink to a directory? $src readable but a FIFO?
- Does anything in the change break if `$dst`'s parent is a symlink, or if `$HOME` contains a space?
- Anything in tests/steam-env.sh that still passes for the wrong reason, especially among the four new cases.

Rate EVERY finding Critical, Important, or nit, and say explicitly if a category has none. Prefer few sharp findings.

input.prompt:
You are a READ-ONLY skeptical reviewer (documentation accuracy + verification). Write nothing — no files, no mutating git commands.

Repo: /home/sauyon/devel/dotfiles/.drovr/wt/steam-nix-env (git worktree, branch drovr/steam-nix-env). Working tree clean.
Range: `git diff 10fabaf..HEAD` — one commit, 814e4fa. Read the full commit message too (`git log -1 814e4fa`).

This is ROUND 3. Two earlier rounds found that several comments stated mechanisms BACKWARDS or cited the wrong line numbers, and those were corrected. This repo's README says "a comment claiming the model is right proves nothing", so prose accuracy is a first-class defect class here. Your job: verify the CURRENT claims, including the newly-written corrections, against the real machine, read-only. Assume the corrections may have introduced new errors.

Verify each of these, and say VERIFIED or give the correct version:
1. "Arch's ld.so *defines* __pointer_chk_guard@@GLIBC_PRIVATE and Arch's libc.so.6 (2.44) leaves it *undefined*... nix's glibc 2.42 defines it in neither." Check with `nm -D`.   The comment-before-`[Desktop Entry]` worry is unfounded, and I checked it empirically rather than from the spec alone:
  
  - Two files already shipped in `/usr/share/applications` on this host start with `#` comment lines before the group header: `/usr/share/applications/vim.desktop` (two comment lines) and `/usr/share/applications/lstopo.desktop`. Both are in the live launcher database.

  - Spec text matches: "Lines beginning with a # ... are considered comments". GLib's GKeyFile (what `xdg-open`/`gio`/every GTK launcher parses with) skips leading comments before the first group.
  
  I could not run `desktop-file-validate` on the *generated* file (it requires a regular file path — `/dev/stdin` and process substitution are both rejected — and I am not permitted to write one), but the vim.desktop precedent is the same structure and is stronger evidence than a synthetic file would be. The header comment's claim is accurate.
  
  ### Critical
  
  **None.**
  
  ### Important
  
  **I1. `tests/steam-env.sh` argument-ORDER case: `at()` returns `0` for "not found", so the case cannot detect a missing path, and it spuriously FAILS in the documented `$1` mode.**
  
  `/home/sauyon/devel/dotfiles/.drovr/wt/steam-nix-env/tests/steam-env.sh` (the `at()` helper and the order assertion, ~lines 246-264).
  
  `awk '{ print index($0, s) }'` prints `0` when the needle is absent — never an empty string (confirmed: `echo x | awk -v s=nope '{print index($0,s)}'` → `0`). Three consequences:
  
  1. `[ -n "$src_at" ]` is *always* true, and `${src_at:-absent}` in the failure message can never print `absent` — the guard and the diagnostic are both dead.
  2. Because `0 -lt "$dst_at"` is true, the case passes when the src argument is **absent entirely**. No other case greps the activation blob for `/usr/share/applications/steam.desktop`, so a regression that dropped or renamed argument 1 (e.g. to `steam2.desktop`) passes all 42 cases. This is precisely the "passes for the wrong reason" class, in the newest case. (Transposition itself *is* still caught — `src_at > dst_at` — so the case's headline purpose survives; it's the absent/renamed variant that slips through.)
  3. The reverse asymmetry is a real spurious failure: in `./tests/steam-env.sh /path/to/steam` mode `WRAPPER_STORE=""`, so `at "${WRAPPER_STORE:-/nix/store}/bin/steam"` searches for the literal `/nix/store/bin/steam`, gets `0`, and `[ "$dst_at" -lt 0 ]` is false → the case reports FAILED and the suite exits 1. The sibling "activation points at the same wrapper" case has an explicit `skip` for exactly this mode; this one forgot it. Same hazard if `xdg.dataHome` is ever non-default, since the test hardcodes `$HOME/.local/share/...` instead of deriving it: `dst_at` would be `0` and the case would fail for a reason unrelated to ordering.
  
  Fix shape: have `at()` emit empty (or a sentinel) on `index()==0`, require all three to be non-zero explicitly, and `skip` the ordering case when `WRAPPER_STORE` is empty.
  
  **I2. On a refusal, the stale override is left in place — reproducing the exact "dead Exec= that looks right and silently does nothing" state the header calls the worst shape available.**
  
  `home/steam-desktop-override`, both post-condition branches (and the `-d "$dst"` / bad-`$exe` refusals).

The assertion itself is right.

Two lower-value test weaknesses.** (a) The `steam.desktop.backup` case discards the exit status, so it passes on any regression that makes the script fail *before* the sweep; the neighbouring cases explain why they check status, and this one should too. (b) Nothing validates the generated file as a desktop entry — given the marker is the new risk surface, a `command -v desktop-file-validate >/dev/null && desktop-file-validate "$out"` case (skip when absent; it *is* present on this host) would pin the property I had to verify by proxy above.
